title: Interpretation not shown well-defined up to alpha-equivalence

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Terms are taken up to α-equivalence (solution.tex:49, 234) and the domain of # is Λ_→ (α-classes), yet the interpretation is defined by raw recursion on M with "Rename z fresh" (solution.tex:303) and no lemma establishing that ⟦λz.P⟧_ρ is independent of the chosen bound-variable name. Hence it is not established that the recursion descends to α-equivalence classes, so #:Λ_→→Ord is not yet shown to be a well-defined function on the stated domain.

FIX: Add an α-invariance lemma: for z′ fresh, ⟦λz.P⟧_ρ = ⟦λz′.P[z:=z′]⟧_ρ. Prove by structural induction (the body ⟦P⟧_{ρ[z:=a]} and the shift 1+‖a‖_σ both depend only on the argument VALUE a, not on the name z). Combine with the Coincidence Lemma to conclude ⟦·⟧ and # are well-defined on α-classes.

Difficulty: easy/routine; no conceptual obstacle.
